title: Enhanced charging in open Rabi and Dicke quantum batteries
authors: A-Long Zhou, Nuo Xu, Ya-Wen Xiao, Li-Li Gao, Long-Jie Li, Zi-Min Li, Chuan-Cun Shu
abstract: We investigate open-system charging protocols for Rabi and Dicke quantum batteries under direct incoherent pumping. The charging dynamics follows a Lindblad master equation, while effective non-Hermitian generators describe the conditioned no-jump mechanism. For a single Rabi battery, this pumping suppresses coherent energy backflow, broadens the high-energy charging window, and improves robustness against both timing errors and detuning. At the selected Rabi operating points, pumping also increases ergotropy and the extractable fraction of the stored energy. For finite Dicke batteries, direct incoherent pumping likewise stabilizes the charging dynamics. Across the finite-size scan, the strongest pump considered improves the peak stored energy and ergotropy per cell and near-peak timing robustness relative to the Hermitian reference. The maximum average charging power also increases, although this metric includes pump-assisted jump contributions. Equal-input comparisons show that the relative performance of common-cavity Dicke and independent Rabi batteries varies with the pump-input bound. Taken together, these results show that direct incoherent pumping provides a route to stabilized charging in Rabi and finite Dicke quantum batteries.
summary: This paper analyzes how direct incoherent pumping enhances the charging capabilities of Rabi and Dicke quantum batteries. Using the Lindblad master equation, the authors show that pumping stabilizes energy storage and increases extractable energy (ergotropy) in these open quantum systems. The findings provide a theoretical route for improving quantum energy harvesting in cavity QED setups.
main_problem: The paper investigates enhanced charging protocols for Rabi and Dicke quantum batteries operating in open quantum systems subjected to direct incoherent pumping.
main_result: Direct incoherent pumping stabilizes the charging dynamics in both Rabi and finite Dicke quantum batteries, improving stored energy, ergotropy, and robustness against errors compared to Hermitian references.
method: The dynamics are modeled using the Lindblad master equation, supplemented by analysis using effective non-Hermitian generators for the conditioned no-jump mechanism.
model_or_system: The models include the Rabi battery (TLS coupled to a single bosonic mode) and the Dicke battery (N coupled TLSs to a common bosonic mode). The dynamics are governed by Hamiltonians and Lindblad dissipation terms.
key_observables: Charging Energy ($\Delta E$), Average Charging Power ($\Delta P$), Maximum Stored Energy ($\Delta E_{\max}$), Ergotropy ($W$), and Timing Robustness ($R_{0.95}$).
important_parameters: Pumping rate ($\gamma$), coupling strength ($g$), detuning ($\Delta$), and the pump-input bound.
main_assumptions: The analysis distinguishes between the full Lindblad evolution and the auxiliary conditioned no-jump descriptions; approximations include the Rotating-Wave Approximation (RWA) in some contexts.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the open quantum battery models (Rabi and Dicke) under direct incoherent pumping.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework using the Lindblad master equation to track charging metrics. It then analyzes the specific behavior of the Rabi and Dicke models, comparing pumping effects against Hermitian limits and examining various performance diagnostics.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses open quantum system dynamics, energy storage, and non-equilibrium physics in quantum optics, making it highly relevant for AMO theorists studying cavity QED and quantum energy harvesting.
